document: LinkedIn framework: Contrarian belief -> why people believe it -> hidden cost -> better belief -> concrete example -> soft CTA. Use when the audience has a common but limiting assumption.
LinkedIn framework: Symptom -> real diagnosis -> why common fixes fail -> 3-part better approach -> what to do first -> CTA. Use when the audience feels stuck but misidentifies the cause.
LinkedIn framework: Short scene -> tension -> decision -> result -> lesson -> audience application -> CTA. Keep story details specific and tie the lesson back to the reader's problem.

Instagram carousel framework: Slide 1 bold mistake hook -> slides 2-4 specific mistakes -> slides 5-7 fixes -> slide 8 quick checklist -> slide 9 CTA to save/comment. Each slide should carry one clear idea.
Instagram how-to framework: Promise one small outcome -> show 3 concise steps -> give an example -> name common trap -> CTA to save or comment keyword for template.
Instagram story framework: Relatable problem -> quick poll -> short tip -> proof or example -> DM keyword CTA. Use for lightweight engagement and lead flow entry points.

Authority framework: Claim -> proof from experience -> what most people miss -> practical takeaway -> CTA. The proof can be a client pattern, repeated observation, data point, or before-after example.
Objection framework: Quote the objection -> validate why it feels true -> reframe the risk -> show lower-friction path -> invite reply/comment. Use for skeptical audiences.
Checklist framework: Name task -> list 5-7 checks -> explain the highest-leverage check -> tell the reader when to use it -> CTA to save or request the full version.
Transformation framework: Before state -> friction and emotion -> turning point -> after state -> bridge steps -> CTA. Make the before state vivid enough that the reader recognizes themselves.
